caption:
The people who change the world are usually the ones who were told they were “too much,” “too unrealistic,” or “doing life wrong.”

Your brain was not designed to find your purpose by copying everyone else.

The moment you stop blindly following the script you were handed, you stop living on autopilot.

💖🧠 Em 

#neuroscience #growthmindset
author: Emily McDonald
transcript: Science shows that you actually have to break the rules if you want to be successful. And I'll tell you the neuroscience behind why. Every time you play the game of life by someone else's rules, you do what's expected of you, what you should do, or what's realistic. You're training your brain to stay small. Playing it safe wires your brain for mediocrity. And it takes you out of your authenticity, which is where you are the most magnetic. But when you start playing by your own rules and taking risks, your brain shifts. You activate exploratory networks in your brain instead of repetitive survival loops, which boosts dopamine and motivation because you're actually choosing your path. You strengthen your prefrontal cortex so that you can actually be the boss of your own life. You also shake up the default mode network, which gets you out of autopilot and into being the creator of your life. Feeling like you have agency over your own life is one of the strongest predictors of well-being. And when you're following everyone else's rules, you don't have that. Creativity literally requires deviation from established patterns. That's why every visionary looks delusional before they look successful. Following the rules might get you a normal life, but it's not the norm to be happy and feel fulfilled. That's why there's so many haters in this world. Life is a game, and the people who win are not the ones who follow the rules. They're the ones who rewrite them. You cannot use someone else's map to find yourself.
title: Break Rules to Wire Your Brain for Success
one_liner: Playing by your own rules activates dopamine and agency, while following others wires your brain for mediocrity.
key_points: Following others' rules trains repetitive survival loops, suppressing motivation and authenticity
Taking personal risks activates exploratory brain networks and boosts dopamine
Breaking from the expected strengthens the prefrontal cortex and disrupts autopilot (default mode network)
Perceived agency over your life is one of the strongest predictors of well-being
